passages.quote: The metallic bellows is most accurate when measuring pressures from 0.5 to 75 psig.
The bellows is a one-piece, collapsible, seamless metallic unit that has deep folds formed from very thin-walled tubing.
System pressure is applied to the internal volume of the bellows.
As the bellows and linkage assembly moves, either an electrical signal is generated or a direct pressure indication is provided.
in practice, the bellows must always be opposed by a spring
This change in cross-section causes the tube to straighten slightly.
the movement of the tip of the tube can then be used to position a pointer or to develop an equivalent electrical signal
all pressure detectors are used to provide up to three basic functions: indication, alarm, and control.
If a pressure instrument fails, spare detector elements may be utilized if installed.
the pressure may be read at an independent local mechanical gauge, if available, or a precision pressure gauge may be installed in the system at a convenient point.
Pressure instruments are sensitive to variations in the atmospheric pressure surrounding the detector.
Ambient temperature variations will affect the accuracy and reliability of pressure detection instrumentation.
The presence of humidity will also affect most electrical equipment, especially electronic equipment.
Transducers can produce a change in resistance, inductance, or capacitance.
A strain gauge measures the external force (pressure) applied to a fine wire.
The pressure change causes a resistance change due to the distortion of the wire.
As the wire grid is distorted by elastic deformation, its length is increased, and its cross-sectional area decreases.
This change in resistance is used as the variable resistance in a bridge circuit that provides an electrical signal for indication of pressure.
The temperature compensating gauge compensates for the heat produced by current flowing through the fine wire of the strain gauge.
The balancing motor moves the slider along the slidewire, restoring the bridge to a balanced condition.
The inductance-type transducer consists of three parts: a coil, a movable magnetic core, and a pressure sensing element.
When the core is in the mid-position, there is no secondary output.
consist of two flexible conductive plates and a dielectric.
As pressure increases, the flexible conductive plates will move farther apart, changing the capacitance of the transducer.
The sensing element senses the pressure of the monitored system and converts the pressure to a mechanical signal.
The transducer converts the mechanical signal to an electrical signal that is proportional to system pressure.
The detector circuitry will amplify and/or transmit this signal to the pressure indicator.
The pressure indicator provides remote indication of the system pressure being measured.

body.text: With a heavy range spring, some bellows can measure pressures of over 1000 psig.
As inlet pressure varies, the bellows expands or contracts. Its moving end is connected to a mechanical linkage assembly.

The fluid flows through a venturi

checks.q: In what range is the metallic bellows most accurate?
checks.x: The metallic bellows is most accurate when measuring pressures from 0.5 to 75 psig.

body.text: The bourdon tube is a thin-walled tube flattened to an elliptical cross-section and bent lengthwise into an arc of 270 to 300 degrees.

body.alt: Curved bourdon tube fixed at one end, with its tip linked to a pointer on a scale.

body.text: Pressure inside the tube causes distention of the flat sections and tends to restore its original round cross-section.
Since the tube is fastened at one end, the tip traces a curve.

checks.q: What happens to a bourdon tube as internal pressure increases?
checks.x: The change in cross-section causes the tube to straighten slightly.

body.text: Other resistance-type transducers combine a bellows or bourdon tube with a variable resistor. As the bellows moves, the slider changes the resistance.

body.alt: Center-tapped coil with a movable magnetic core.

body.text: As the element moves the core inside the coil, the coil's inductance changes. Current through the coil increases as inductance decreases.

body.alt: Differential transformer: a primary coil around the center of a tube, secondary coils at each end, and a movable core.

body.text: The lesson plan gives two failure modes for pressure detectors. Overpressurization can damage sensing elements, and the detector fails high.
body.cite: Word: Pressure Detectors.docx, slide 1.16 Pressure Detector Failures

body.text: A sensing element leak or rupture causes the detector to fail low.
body.cite: Word: Pressure Detectors.docx, slide 1.16 Pressure Detector Failures

body.text: A weakened spring in a detector has to compress further to give the same counterforce, so indicated pressure increases.

checks.q: A sensing element in a pressure detector ruptures. How does the detector fail?
checks.x: A sensing element leak or rupture fails low.

checks.q: A pressure detector is overpressurized. How does it fail?
checks.x: Overpressurization fails high and can damage sensing elements.

facts.a: A thin-walled, flattened tube bent into an arc. Pressure inside tends to straighten it, and the tip movement positions a pointer or develops a signal.

facts.q: What are the three environmental concerns for pressure instruments?
facts.a: Atmospheric pressure, ambient temperature, and humidity.

facts.q: What must oppose a metallic bellows in practice?
facts.a: A spring, so the bellows' travel stays on the compression side.

facts.q: What does a strain gauge measure?
facts.a: The pressure applied to a fine wire, through the resistance change caused by distortion of the wire.

facts.q: What three kinds of change can a pressure transducer produce?
facts.a: A change in resistance, inductance, or capacitance.

summary.text: In a bellows detector, pressure moves the bellows and linkage to produce a signal or move a pointer.
In a bourdon tube detector, pressure tends to restore the tube's round cross-section, so the tube straightens and its tip moves.
Pressure detectors perform indication, alarm, and control functions.
A strain gauge's change in resistance is used in a bridge circuit that provides a signal for indication of pressure.
A typical device goes from sensing element to transducer, detector circuitry, and pressure indicator.
